name: Content Freshness
description: Checks whether the page exposes machine-readable publish and modified dates via article:published_time / article:modified_time meta, JSON-LD datePublished / dateModified, or <time datetime> elements. Dates let AI engines judge recency when choosing sources to cite. It does not evaluate how old the dates are.

scoring.summary: Page scope. Publish date found if article:published_time has content, any JSON-LD block contains a truthy datePublished at any depth, or a <time datetime> is labelled as the publish date (itemprop="datePublished", or class published/pubdate/post-date/entry-date on it or its parent). Modified date found if article:modified_time has content, any JSON-LD block contains a truthy dateModified at any depth, or any other <time datetime> element exists. Neither => 0. Otherwise start at 5 and subtract 2 for whichever is missing. Result: both => 5; one only => 3.

rules.condition: JSON-LD: each script[type="application/ld+json"] parsed (template tags substituted first; invalid JSON skipped silently); recursive search of objects and arrays for own property 'datePublished' / 'dateModified' with truthy value. A template-built block that still cannot be parsed counts when its raw text contains the property name (predicted).

time[datetime] elements: one labelled as the publish date (itemprop="datePublished" or class published/pubdate/post-date/entry-date on it or its parent) is a PUBLISH signal; every other one is a MODIFIED signal
foundPublish = hasPublishDate || hasJsonLdPublish || labelled publish <time>; foundModified = hasModifiedDate || hasJsonLdModified || other <time datetime>

scoring.status_mapping: Engine rule on the integer score: 5 pass, 3 warning (60%), 0 fail. Same outcome as the extension.

detect.source_procedure: Script checks/content/freshness.mjs runs on every HTML page the site model loads (built output or static HTML): meta article:published_time / article:modified_time, JSON-LD via lib/jsonld.mjs (template tags substituted), and time[datetime] elements. For unbuilt framework sources, build first; dates injected at runtime are not visible.

parity.note: Signals are usually template-driven and conditional (only on article pages, only when front matter has dates), so source analysis must resolve which templates apply to which pages. JSON-LD or <time> elements injected by JS, CMS content, or third-party widgets (e.g. comment timestamps with <time datetime>) are visible to the extension but not the repo. Any <time datetime> anywhere on the page (even in a footer or widget) counts as a modified date.

fix_summary: Emit both dates: add article:published_time and article:modified_time meta (or Next.js metadata.openGraph publishedTime/modifiedTime, Hugo _internal/opengraph.html with date/lastmod), and/or JSON-LD datePublished/dateModified, and render <time datetime="..."> for the updated date in the article template. Wiring templates is automatic; real date values come from front matter or git history and may need user confirmation.

divergences.extension: Any <time datetime> counts as a modified-date signal, so a page whose only date is a publish <time> reports 'modified found, publish missing'.
divergences.plugin: A <time> explicitly labelled as the publish date (itemprop="datePublished" or a published/pubdate/post-date/entry-date class on it or its parent) counts as the publish date; unlabelled ones keep the extension behaviour.
divergences.reason: Bug: the finding named the wrong missing date. The score is unchanged in that case (3).

divergences.extension: Reads the rendered page, where template tags are filled in; invalid JSON-LD is skipped.
divergences.plugin: JSON-LD template tags are substituted before parsing; a template-built block that still cannot be parsed counts a date property present in its raw text. Such results are marked predicted.
divergences.reason: Source vs live: never score a site down for a template value the repo cannot show.
